newsitem.title: INDIA: India has no plan to raise oil prices - minister.
newsitem.headline: India has no plan to raise oil prices - minister.

text.p: Indian Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu said on Friday that the government has no plan to raise the domestic prices of petroleum products.
"Actually there is no hike of prices. We are not intending to hike the price of petroleum products," Balu told Asian News International (ANI), a local news agency.

The minister said the government would owe state-controlled oil firms 158 billion rupees ($4.4 billion) by the end of March. The firms have been pressing Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government to raise the funds needed to repay the money by increasing prices.
The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Balu as telling reporters that "the deficit will have to be managed by some other means".
Balu told ANI: "Let us see what happens in the budget." He was referring to the government's budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year starting on April 1, to be presented to parliament later on Friday.
